import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Calculate total spending on all products
df['Total_Spending'] = df['MntWines'] + df['MntFruits'] + df['MntMeatProducts'] + \
                       df['MntFishProducts'] + df['MntSweetProducts'] + df['MntGoldProds']

# Drop rows with missing income for a cleaner visualization, as income is central to this plot
df_cleaned = df.dropna(subset=['Income'])

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create the scatter plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df_cleaned,
    x='Income',
    y='Total_Spending',
    hue='Education',
    size='Total_Spending', # Use total spending for point size to visually emphasize higher spending
    sizes=(50, 1000), # Range of sizes for points
    alpha=0.7,
    palette='viridis', # A perceptually uniform colormap
    edgecolor='w', # White edges for points for better separation
    linewidth=0.5
)

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Customer Spending vs. Income by Education Level', fontsize=18, fontweight='bold')
plt.xlabel('Annual Income', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Total Spending on Products', fontsize=14)

# Improve legend title and position
plt.legend(title='Education Level', title_fontsize='13', fontsize='11',

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Calculate total spending on all products
df['Total_Spending'] = df['MntWines'] + df['MntFruits'] + df['MntMeatProducts'] + \
                       df['MntFishProducts'] + df['MntSweetProducts'] + df['MntGoldProds']

# Drop rows with missing income for a cleaner visualization, as income is central to this plot
df_cleaned = df.dropna(subset=['Income'])

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create the scatter plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df_cleaned,
    x='Income',
    y='Total_Spending',
    hue='Education',
    size='Total_Spending', # Use total spending for point size to visually emphasize higher spending
    sizes=(50, 1000), # Range of sizes for points
    alpha=0.7,
    palette='viridis', # A perceptually uniform colormap
    edgecolor='w', # White edges for points for better separation
    linewidth=0.5
)

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Customer Spending vs. Income by Education Level', fontsize=18, fontweight='bold')
plt.xlabel('Annual Income', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Total Spending on Products', fontsize=14)

# Improve legend title and position
plt.legend(title='Education Level', title_fontsize='13', fontsize='11',
           bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)

# Customize x and y axis ticks for better readability
plt.ticklabel_format(style='plain', axis='x') # Prevent scientific notation for income
plt.ticklabel_format(style='plain', axis='y') # Prevent scientific notation for spending

# Adjust layout to prevent labels/legend from being cut off
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.88, 1]) # Adjust rect to make space for the legend

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
